author: C (Claude Code, independent validator and integration tester)

owners.A: Codex A: backend recovery, context efficiency, persisted agent reports
owners.C: Claude Code: regression tests, combined qualification, the bounded live Gemini test, demonstration evidence

statement: Acceptance checklist for the Deep Agents completion sprint. A status is assigned only from behaviour observed on a named commit in a named lane. A missing producer is never a pass. This profile does not replace predicates.v1 or the narrow demo profile and implies no general scientific proof.

lanes.controlled: Controlled model decisions (offline fixture policy, zero provider requests) with the actual graph, routes, worker and authority.
lanes.real_science: As controlled, plus actual Counterdex execution, native evidence and replay.
lanes.live_gemini: Actual Gemini through the metered gateway and reserve-before-dispatch ledger; FREE TIER ONLY; sprint ceiling 12 physical requests including failed and uncertain attempts; no automatic retry or fallback; public or synthetic inputs only.
lanes.historical_replay: Fresh native replay of retained artifacts with the matching Counterdex runtime.

rules: Controlled, real-science, live and replay results are recorded separately; a controlled run is never labelled live.
Frozen predicates and expected results are not weakened to obtain a pass; a correction is a new profile version.
Adaptivity is graded as acceptable sets of next actions per evidence condition, not exact wording or tool order.
A live PASS needs ledger attempts with execution_mode live, provider gemini and recorded usage, and model-issued tool calls that the graph executed.
If a live run exposes a defect, live traffic stops until an offline regression demonstrates the fix.

items.claim: The preferred UI invokes the actual Deep Agents coordinator.
items.pass: Driving the preferred browser interface creates a DB-RESEARCH-1 session and advances it; the ordinary worker runs the compiled create_deep_agent graph, whose recorded tool events and research-plan.v1 revision belong to that session. A mockup, fixture events or a direct API script do not pass.

items.claim: Gemini actually selects and uses tools.
items.pass: In the live lane, genuine provider responses contain function calls (write_todos and at least one research tool) that the graph executes, each turn preceded by a reserved ledger attempt with provider gemini, execution_mode live and recorded usage.

items.claim: Scientific evidence changes the next action.
items.pass: Sessions differing only in the reviewed claim or returned evidence take different next actions from the acceptable sets: a checked counterexample leads to a separately approved pair-design review; no counterexample or unresolved leads to an assumption review or honest stop, never a design. Missing inputs lead to clarification without science.

No scientific child exists before the canonical decision; the dispatched child binds the approved review id and digest; rejection, forged, stale or edited decisions and raw graph commands create no child; design requires its own approval.

items.claim: Interrupted work recovers without duplicate computation.
items.pass: Interrupting the worker after a child is reserved or dispatched and restarting it continues or reconciles the same action: child jobs and scientific reservations do not increase, duplicate resume or decision returns the existing action, and evidence is preserved.

items.claim: Validated explanations and recommendations reach downloaded reports.
items.pass: The downloaded research report contains the agent's explanation and next-step recommendation, each bound to cited evidence ids that exist in the report; unsupported or ungrounded statements are withheld or marked; the report never upgrades a tier or claims proof.

items.claim: Science remains accessible after model failure.
items.pass: After a completed child, a model failure (including a provider error) leaves evidence, report snapshot, native bytes, anchor and fresh replay intact and the recorded outcome unchanged.

items.claim: Quota exhaustion is clear and triggers no fallback or retry.
items.pass: A provider 429 or an exhausted session allocation produces one charged attempt (or none when refused before dispatch), a stable error code the UI shows in plain language, no second provider request, no switch to the controlled policy or another model, and no scientific child.

items.claim: One small investigation runs through the preferred browser interface and the Gemini-backed graph.
items.pass: ACC-02 observed in the browser journey; approved science executes; returned evidence reaches the model (a later live turn's input contains the evidence id); a grounded report is retained.

items.claim: A contrasting live case changes the next action.
items.pass: A live session with missing inputs or an inconclusive result takes a different permitted next action than LIVE-01.

items.claim: The follow-up design path runs live within the remaining limit.
items.pass: A live advance after LIVE-01's report proposes a separate pair-design review that executes only after its own approval.

items.claim: One integrated commit containing both owners' changes passes combined qualification.
items.pass: On that commit in isolated stores and ports: refresh/reopen, approval rejection, duplicate resume, interruption recovery, report binding, native download and replay, and evidence preservation after provider failure; the relevant release checks pass once.
